evals.prompt:
Which should I go for, just the top two? I've worked in hotels for six years, front desk first and night manager for the last two at a 70-room hotel. I run a team of four on nights and do the rota and the end-of-night reports. I want to get back to working days.

1. Guest Services Manager, The Marlowe, Penhallow - lead the front desk and concierge team at a 120-room hotel.
2. Night Manager, Harbourside Lodge - overnight sole charge of a 90-room hotel, four nights on, four off.
3. Reservations Supervisor, Ferrand Hotels - run a team of five handling group and online bookings, Monday to Friday days.
4. Bar and Events Manager, The Old Mill Inn - personal licence holder required; run the bar and the weekend weddings.
5. Revenue Analyst, Ferrand Hotels - set room rates using our revenue system; degree in a numerate subject preferred.
6. Housekeeping Supervisor, The Marlowe, Penhallow - supervise 12 room attendants, early starts from 6am.
assertions: It names exactly two roles as its picks, not a ranked list of all six
Night Manager is not one of the two picks, because the person said they want to work days
Bar and Events Manager is not a pick unless the reply names the personal licence as a question to settle first, since the person did not say they hold one
It says the picks rest on one-line descriptions rather than full postings, and that the full postings should be read before applying
It does not state any requirement, duty, pay or hours for a role beyond what that role's one line says
It says in a line or so that the other four were looked at, without a full write-up of each
It delivers the two picks from what was given, and does not refuse or stop to ask for a CV or the postings first
It gives no percentage or match score, and does not credit the person with a qualification, licence or system they did not mention

evals.prompt: I'm a heavy diesel tech looking to move on from my current workshop. I saved Brackwater Freight's careers page as brackwater-careers.html and exported my saved TradesBoard listings as tradesboard-export.csv. My CV is mere-castell-cv.md. Which of these should I apply for? I'm staying in Tarnhaven: Marrowby and Port Halloran are both under an hour's drive, Kestrel Flats is about three and a half hours away. Give me my top three at most, ranked, and just a line on each of the others so I know why not. I'll be reading it on my phone at smoko so keep it tight.
assertions: It recommends no more than three roles, and covers each of the other roles in about a line, not a full write-up

Every role it recommends is one of the Brackwater Heavy Diesel Technician at Tarnhaven (HDT-0412), the Tolley Earthmoving Hydraulics Technician, or the Marrowby Truck & Trailer Brake & Suspension Technician, and it does not set the Tolley or Marrowby role aside over items those postings list only as preferred or desirable (excavator experience, a forklift certificate, CoF inspection experience)

It rules out the Brackwater Senior Fleet Technician because night shifts are a required part of its roster and the CV says day shift only, even though the pay and experience fit; and it rules out the Halloran Haulage Mobile Service Technician (Class 4 licence required at start, she holds Class 2), the Kestrel Flats Workshop Supervisor (must live within 30 minutes of the site, no relocation, and she is staying in Tarnhaven), and the Fleet Reliability Engineer (a mechanical engineering degree is required and the CV shows a trade certificate)

It treats the Brackwater Heavy Diesel Technician on the careers page and the TradesBoard 'Heavy Diesel Mechanic (Tarnhaven depot)' listing as one role (both are ref HDT-0412), not two, while keeping the Port Halloran Heavy Diesel Technician (HDT-0431) as a separate role

For the Port Halloran Heavy Diesel Technician (HDT-0431) it says the saved page has only the title and a link, not the posting, and neither recommends it nor rules it out on the title alone; it suggests reading the full posting first
It accounts for all eight distinct roles across the two files: the three Brackwater featured roles, the Port Halloran listing, and the four other TradesBoard listings

It does not credit Mere with anything her CV does not show, such as a Class 4 licence, an engineering degree, a forklift certificate, CoF inspection experience, supervisory experience beyond mentoring one apprentice, or availability for nights, and it does not state what the Port Halloran posting says

evals.prompt:
ok so my cousin sent me these from the local jobs group, which 2 should i actually go for?? 2 max, i dont have time to do more applications than that

me: line cook 3 yrs at a pub kitchen in Dunmore Quay, food safety level 2 cert, no car so its the bus or nothing, and im on notice til 15 nov so cant start before that

1. Commis chef - The Lantern Room, Dunmore Quay. 4 nights a wk, €15.10/hr, 1 yr kitchen exp, start asap
2. Breakfast cook, Gullhaven Hotel (Gullhaven). 6am starts, own transport essential (no bus out there before 7). 2 yrs exp, €15.80
3. chef de partie - Saltmarsh Bistro, Dunmore Quay. 2+ yrs line experience, food safety level 2. starting december. €16.40/hr
4. Lantern Room Dunmore Quay - commis chef, 4 nights/week, 15.10 ph, kitchen exp 1yr+, start ASAP!!
5. Head chef, Copperline Catering. food safety level 3 required + 5 yrs supervisory experience, €48k
6. kitchen porter/cook - Brindle Café, he only sent the link: https://jobs.example.com/brindle-kp
assertions: It picks no more than two roles, as asked, and keeps the reply short to match the quick question
It recognises that postings 1 and 4 are the same Lantern Room commis chef job and does not count them as two roles or use them as both picks
Its picks include the Saltmarsh Bistro chef de partie, and neither pick is the Gullhaven Hotel, Copperline Catering or Brindle Café job

It says the Gullhaven Hotel job is out because own transport is essential with 6am starts and there is no bus before 7, and the Copperline head chef job is out because it requires a level 3 food safety certificate and five years' supervisory experience, which the person doesn't have
For the Brindle Café job it says only a link was given, so the posting hasn't been read and the job can't be judged from its title; it neither recommends it nor rules it out

It points out that the Lantern Room wants someone to start as soon as possible while the person can't start until after 15 November, as something to raise or weigh, rather than treating the start date as fine

It does not credit the person with anything they didn't say, such as a car or driving licence, a level 3 food safety certificate, supervisory or chef de partie experience, or more than three years in kitchens, and it does not claim to know what the Brindle Café posting says
